To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ranked set sample variance estimator is the best unbiased estimator of the population variance when the distribution is symmetric.
the ranked set sampling procedure can be an improvement over simple random sampling for estimating the mean and variance of location-scale distributions.
for the location-scale models considered, the best unbiased estimators are the same as the corresponding maximum likelihood estimators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the estimation of population parameters for location-scale families of symmetric distributions.
the development of improved estimators of the population mean for a variety of location-scale distributions, and the identification of those estimators which are optimal for a given distribution.
improving estimation procedures based on the ranked set sampling procedure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the normal distribution, the best estimator of the population variance is based on the sample variance from a simple random sample, and for the other location-scale distributions, the best estimators of the population mean are based on the sample mean from a simple random or ranked set sample, depending on the sample size.
the estimator of population mean based on ranked set samples is more efficient than the usual estimator based on simple random samples.
for a given distribution from the location-scale family, there is a best unbiased estimator of the population variance, and a ranked set sample can be used to estimate it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for the location-scale distributions with a finite variance and finite Fisher information, the ranked set sample estimator of the mean has an asymptotic relative efficiency of at least 0.75 compared with the usual estimator of the mean, and the ranked set sample estimators of the variance and standard deviation have an asymptotic relative efficiencies of at least 1 compared with the usual estimators.

, when a population is known to be from a location-scale family, the best estimator of the population variance is a function of the ranked set sample mean and variance, while the best estimator of mean is a linear function of the ranked sample mean and the sample median.
the best estimator is the one based on the mean of the smallest observations from each of the independent ranked set samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the location-scale distributions, ranked set sampling can provide improved estimators of the population mean.
, in many cases, the best estimator is the same as the one obtained under the normal model.
the ranked set sample mean and variance estimators are more efficient than the ordinary sample mean and variance estimator for a wide range of location-scale distributions.
